parties:
Afazuddin and others ------ Petitioner
Vs.
District Judge, Cox''s Bazar and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
A M Mahmudur Rahman, J: The petitioners by this petition impugns the order of the learned District Judge, Cox's Bazar dismissing the Misc. Case No. 2 of 1992 filed under Section 134(5) of the Co-operative Society Ordinance, 1984. 

 2. The petitioner 1 is a member of Badarkhali Krishi and Upanibash Samity. He alleges that petitioner 2 is his son and the respondent 2 forcibly constructed a but in his plot No. 191. For this a salish was held under the bye-law of the Badarkhali Krishi and Upanibash Samity. In the salish a decision was taken was refusing restoration of possession of the plot and direction was given for making an awaz deed between the parties regarding the land. An appeal was taken against said order of the salish before the Chairman of the Samity and it was dismissed. Thereafter, the petitioner filed a dispute case under section 84 and 86 of the Co-operative Society Ordinance, 1984 before the District Judge, Cox's Bazar. The dispute case was rejected on the ground of both maintainability mid on merit. The petitioners having lost before the District Judge preferred Appeal No. 10 of 1991 before the Joint Registrar (Judicial). Chittagong. He dismissed the appeal on the ground of limitation. The petitioners then filed Misc. Case No. 2 of 1992 under Section 134(5) of the Ordinance before the District Judge, Cox's Bazar. After hearing the case the learned District Judge dismissed the same on the ground that the case was barred by limitation. 

 3. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the learned District Judge passed the order without jurisdiction. Secondly, there being no provision for awaz in the Ordinance the District Co-operative Officer failed in consider the aspect of the case and as such his order is illegal. Thirdly, Respondent I acted illegally in holding that the appeal is barred by limitation inasmuch as the appeal was filed in time from the dale of knowledge of the petitioner and for the act of God i.e. the cyclone in the locality he could not approach the court in time. 

 4. We have examined the relevant provision of law on limitation prescribed for filing of case of the present nature before the learned District Judge. The prescribed period of limitation for filing appeal from an order passed under Section 86 an 87 of the Co-operative Societies Ordinance, 1984 is one month from the date of knowledge of the decisions. Section 134(3) provides that Section 5 of the Limitation Act shall not be made applicable to an appeal filed under Section 134(1). We do not find any reason to hold that because the petitioner could not file the appeal within prescribed period of limitation within 30 days due to devastating cyclone the petition ought to have been accepted by the learned District Judge on condonation of delay and the learned District Judge dismissed the case illegally holding that the appeal before the appellate authority was time barred. When this Ordinance a special enactment excludes the application of Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay to an appeal it cannot be held that the learned District Judge failed to exercise his jurisdiction vested under Section 134(5) of the Ordinance in not condoning delay in filing the appeal. Where a special enactment expressly provides that for filing an appeal beyond period prescribed provision of Section 5 of the Limitation Act shall not be made applicable the appellate authority before whom the appeal lies has no power to condone delay by applying provision of section 5 of the Limitation Act for accepting the appeal. We do not find that the learned District Judge failed to exercise his jurisdiction in not holding that the appellate authority was wrong in holding that the appeal was time barred. There is no substance in this petition.
